note: Adapted from the English species-level description in Hill (1942); the original describes the alate and the soldier and does not describe the worker. Nomenclatural history: Hagen placed it in Hodotermes (Stolotermes) in 1858, and Froggatt, Desneux, Holmgren and Mjöberg all used Stolotermes brunneicornis; the two records of Froggatt (1905, 1915) were wrongly attributed to Brauer. OCR problems: the heading reads "Stolotermes brunneieornis"; the synonymy list gives "brunneicomis" in several places; "Btoloteriwes" is Stolotermes; "mouth pans" is mouth parts; "sth" is 5th; "arid" is and; "snaller" is smaller; "medial]" is median; there is a stray OCR character before "Slightly"; "l/lO" is 1/10; "3*30" and "4*36" are 3.30 and 4.36; "Pig. 10" is Fig.; "queen standi oils" is queenslandicus; "vietoriensis" is victoriensis. The type locality, Tasmania (Bruni Island / Adventure Bay and others), agrees with the checklist. Distribution and biology (found only in decaying wood in damp places) are not translated into the morphology sections.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The alate can be distinguished from S. victoriensis by its larger size and the large antennal spot; no reliable character has been found in the available material to distinguish the soldier of this species from some individuals of that species. See also S. queenslandicus.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Dark brown; the basal antennal segment, mouthparts, an irregular area in the middle of the frons, the legs, two anterolateral areas and a larger median area of the pronotum dark buff. Head round, sparsely hairy, frons with a large irregular depression. Frontal spot distinct. Median and transverse sutures clear. Antennae 16-segmented; segments 3, 4 and 5 very variable: segments 3 and 4 very small, equal and fused, or segment 3 distinctly smaller than segment 4 and segment 4 sometimes larger than segment 5, or segments 3—7 progressively longer. Compound eyes nearly spherical. Pronotum with a wide, shallowly concave anterior margin, sides rounded and slightly narrowed, posterior margin wide and slightly concave; the anterior margin with a fringe of moderately dense short hairs, the rest with longer, sparser hairs. Wings dark smoky; veins distinct to the tip; the radius reaches the first branch of the radial sector; the radial sector has 7 branches reaching the anterior margin; the media runs in the anterior third of the wing, with 5 branches reaching the posterior margin, some of them branched; the cubitus ends about at the middle of the wing, with 5 branches. Posterior margins of mesonotum and metanotum very wide, straight or slightly concave. Tibial spur formula 3:3:2. Cerci 4-segmented. Measurements: length with wings 13.00 mm (Hagen), length without wings 8.00 mm, head length (to apex of labrum) 1.65—1.76 mm, head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 1.17—1.24 mm, head width 1.50—1.61 mm, greatest diameter of compound eye 0.33—0.36 mm, pronotum length 0.62—0.73 mm, width 1.10—1.24 mm, fore wing length 10.40 mm, width 3.30 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head cadmium yellow, slightly darker in front; labrum, antennae and maxillary palps the same colour as the middle of the head; base of the mandibles the same as the front of the head, the apical third dark rust-coloured; compound eyes more or less pigmented; thorax and abdomen cream-coloured. Head shape variable, often with nearly parallel sides, sometimes widened at the sides, or slightly widened or narrowed in front. Antennae 15—17-segmented; segment 3 and sometimes segment 4 very small and closely fused, segment 4 usually slightly longer than segment 3. Labrum large, widest at the base, slightly narrowed towards the blunt conical tip. Postmentum long and narrow, its narrowest part about one-tenth of the head width. The apical half of the left mandible has two large teeth and one small tooth, the latter far from the large, prominent molar tooth; the apical half of the right mandible has two large teeth and a large basal molar tooth. Pronotum with the anterior and posterior margins wide and shallowly concave, the sides sloping towards the posterior margin, hairs sparse and medium-sized, mainly along the margins. Posterior margins of mesonotum and metanotum broadly truncate; wing pads with a moderate number of hairs, the rest with few hairs. Legs short and stout, sparsely hairy. Tibial spur formula 3:3:2. Measurements: total length 9.25—10.00 mm, head length (to apex of mandibles) 3.85—4.36 mm, head length (to clypeal suture) 2.56—3.06 mm, head width 1.76—1.90 mm, pronotum length 0.58—0.77 mm, width 1.06—1.35 mm.
